descripcion_geo: Motherland of Western Civilization; Their culture and language (koine) formed the world of the New Testament.
importancia_estrategica: Cradle of philosophical thought, the alphabet and the language in which the NT was written.

historias.descripcion: Alexander the Great conquers the known world by spreading the Greek language and culture; Koine Greek becomes the lingua franca of the Mediterranean.
On his second missionary journey, Paul visits Athens and Corinth, the two great cities of Roman Greece.
Paul coordinates a collection in the churches of Greece (Macedonia and Achaia) for the poor of the Jerusalem church.

personajes.descripcion: His conquest Hellenized the world; the NT was written in Greek thanks to his legacy.
He preached the gospel in the heart of Greek culture.
Possibly Greek in origin; wrote the gospel and Acts in literary Greek.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Without Greece there would be no NT: the Greek koine was the vehicle of revelation; Greek philosophy the interlocutor of the gospel.

mitos.nombre: The Septuagint: the Torah in Greek

judaismo.descripcion: The translation of the Torah into Greek (Septuagint, 3rd century BC) was the first bridge between the Hebrew and Hellenistic worlds.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The translation of the Torah into Greek (Septuagint, 3rd century BC) was the first bridge between the Hebrew and Hellenistic worlds.

cristianismo.descripcion: The NT was written entirely in Greek; The Johannine logos dialogues with Greek philosophy (Jn 1:1).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The NT was written entirely in Greek; The Johannine logos dialogues with Greek philosophy (Jn 1:1).

historias.descripcion: The Macedonian's vision redirects Paul's mission towards Greece; the gospel makes the leap to the heart of Western culture.

historias.titulo: Paul in Athens: the Areopagus speech
historias.descripcion: Paul confronts Greek idolatry with monotheism; He quotes Greek poets to announce the resurrection.
Paul writes in Koine Greek for churches throughout the Empire; Greek is the universal language of the gospel.

personajes.descripcion: He preached the gospel in Greece; His letters in Greek are the basis of Christian theology.
Without its Hellenization of the world, the NT would have had no universal language or cultural infrastructure.
Alexandrian Jew, eloquent in the Greek Scriptures; He preached in Achaia.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Greece is the cultural mold of the NT: its language, its philosophy, and its sea routes allowed the spread of the gospel.

cristianismo.descripcion: John 1:1 uses the Greek philosophical concept of 'logos' to announce the incarnate Christ: the gospel speaks in the language of Greek culture.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: John 1:1 uses the Greek philosophical concept of 'logos' to announce the incarnate Christ: the gospel speaks in the language of Greek culture.
